name: kiri
description: A small, fast container runtime for macOS, Windows and Linux
readmeExcerpt:
A tiny, fast container runtime for macOS, Windows and Linux.
Runs your Docker images and works with the docker CLI, Compose and buildx you already use.

Download · Features · Build from source · Releases

--- Kiri is a lightweight replacement for Docker Desktop and OrbStack, written in Rust. It runs containers in one small Linux VM (or straight on the kernel on Linux) and speaks the Docker Engine API, so your tools just work. The name comes from the Igbo word *ntakịrị*, "small". ## Why Kiri - **Fast**: a container starts and exits in about 2.5 ms through the Docker API. That's around 80 times faster than Docker Desktop. - **Light**: the VM sleeps after 60 s idle, the daemon stays at about 15 MB, and it wakes in about 0.15 s. - **Compatible**: `docker`, Compose, buildx, `docker login` and amd64 images through Rosetta. - **Local domains**: `http://.kiri.local`, with HTTPS from Kiri's own certificate authority. - **More than containers**: a one-command Kubernetes cluster and Linux machines. - **A native window** for containers, images, volumes and networks, plus a menu bar item. ## Install | Platform | Get it | |----------|--------| | macOS 14+ (Apple silicon or Intel) | `.dmg` from [runkiri.com/releases](https://runkiri.com/releases/) | | Windows 10 and 11 (x86-64 or Arm, through WSL 2) | `.msi` from [runkiri.com/releases](https://runkiri.com/releases/) | | Linux (Ubuntu, Fedora and others) | `.deb` or `.rpm` from [runkiri.com/releases](https://runkiri.com/releases/) | The first time you open Kiri, it sets up a `kiri` Docker context. Kiri updates itself, and checks each new release's signature first. ## Quick start ```sh docker --context kiri run --rm alpine echo hello docker --context kiri compose up -d kiri k8s start # single-node Kubernetes as the `kiri` kubectl context kiri machine create dev --distro ubuntu && kiri machine shell dev kiri import # bring images, volumes and containers over from OrbStack or Docker Desktop ``` Docker's commands also work as `kiri` commands (`kiri run`, `kiri ps`, `kiri compose up`, and so on), and always target Kiri. ## Numbers `alpine` running `true` and removed, median of 30 runs, same `docker` CLI for all three: | | Docker Engine API | `docker` CLI | |----------------|------------------:|-------------:| | **Kiri** | **2.55 ms** | **14.2 ms** | | Docker Desktop | 213 ms | 243 ms | | OrbStack | 380 ms | 442 ms | Method and every other figure are in [`bench/results.json`](bench/results.json). Rerun with `kiri bench`. ## How it works ``` docker CLI ─┐ compose ────┼─ Docker Engine API ─► kiri daemon ── vsock ──► guest agent (PID 1) buildx ─────┤ owns the VM clone3 → container kiri UI ────┘ ``` The VM uses a custom 10 MB kernel, and its PID 1 is a ~900 KB Rust agent. That agent starts containers with a single `clone3` into namespaces and a cgroup. There's no runc, no shim and no dockerd. More detail is in [docs/development.md](docs/development.md#architecture). ## Documentation - [Features](docs/features.md): everything supported today, release files and known issues - [Development](docs/development.md): building, running from source, architecture and repository layout - [Release notes](docs/releases) ## Roadmap Next is a built-in builder. Kiri will serve Docker's own build endpoints, so buildx uses its docker driver against Kiri as it does against Docker Desktop. This brings `host-gateway` support to BuildKit builds, and images load straight into Kiri. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). To report a vulnerability privately, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). Third-party licences are in [NOTICE](NOTICE). The guest kernel is Linux (GPL-2.0); its config, patches and the source offer are in [`guest/kernel`](guest/kernel). The name "Kiri" and the Kiri logo are not covered by the licence. Forks are welcome, under a different name and logo.
readmeHtml:
A tiny, fast container runtime for macOS, Windows and Linux.
Runs your Docker images and works with the docker CLI, Compose and buildx you already use.

Download · Features · Build from source · Releases

Kiri is a lightweight replacement for Docker Desktop and OrbStack, written in Rust. It runs containers in one small Linux VM (or straight on the kernel on Linux) and speaks the Docker Engine API, so your tools just work.

The name comes from the Igbo word ntakịrị, "small".

Why Kiri

  • Fast: a container starts and exits in about 2.5 ms through the Docker API. That's around 80 times faster than Docker Desktop.
  • Light: the VM sleeps after 60 s idle, the daemon stays at about 15 MB, and it wakes in about 0.15 s.
  • Compatible: docker, Compose, buildx, docker login and amd64 images through Rosetta.
  • Local domains: http://<name>.kiri.local, with HTTPS from Kiri's own certificate authority.
  • More than containers: a one-command Kubernetes cluster and Linux machines.
  • A native window for containers, images, volumes and networks, plus a menu bar item.

Install

Platform Get it
macOS 14+ (Apple silicon or Intel) .dmg from runkiri.com/releases
Windows 10 and 11 (x86-64 or Arm, through WSL 2) .msi from runkiri.com/releases
Linux (Ubuntu, Fedora and others) .deb or .rpm from runkiri.com/releases

The first time you open Kiri, it sets up a kiri Docker context. Kiri updates itself, and checks each new release's signature first.

Quick start

docker --context kiri run --rm alpine echo hello
docker --context kiri compose up -d
kiri k8s start                      # single-node Kubernetes as the `kiri` kubectl context
kiri machine create dev --distro ubuntu && kiri machine shell dev
kiri import                         # bring images, volumes and containers over from OrbStack or Docker Desktop

Docker's commands also work as kiri commands (kiri run, kiri ps, kiri compose up, and so on), and always target Kiri.

Numbers

alpine running true and removed, median of 30 runs, same docker CLI for all three:

Docker Engine API docker CLI
Kiri 2.55 ms 14.2 ms
Docker Desktop 213 ms 243 ms
OrbStack 380 ms 442 ms

Method and every other figure are in bench/results.json. Rerun with kiri bench.

How it works

docker CLI ─┐
compose ────┼─ Docker Engine API ─► kiri daemon ── vsock ──► guest agent (PID 1)
buildx ─────┤                         owns the VM           clone3 → container
kiri UI ────┘

The VM uses a custom 10 MB kernel, and its PID 1 is a ~900 KB Rust agent. That agent starts containers with a single clone3 into namespaces and a cgroup. There's no runc, no shim and no dockerd. More detail is in docs/development.md.

Documentation

  • Features: everything supported today, release files and known issues
  • Development: building, running from source, architecture and repository layout
  • Release notes

Roadmap

Next is a built-in builder. Kiri will serve Docker's own build endpoints, so buildx uses its docker driver against Kiri as it does against Docker Desktop. This brings host-gateway support to BuildKit builds, and images load straight into Kiri.

Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md and the Code of Conduct. To report a vulnerability privately, see SECURITY.md.

License

Apache-2.0. Third-party licences are in NOTICE. The guest kernel is Linux (GPL-2.0); its config, patches and the source offer are in guest/kernel.

The name "Kiri" and the Kiri logo are not covered by the licence. Forks are welcome, under a different name and logo.

releases.name: Kiri 0.1.18
releases.body:
## New
- **A terminal in the window.** Click Terminal in the status bar, or press Control and the backtick key (F4 on Linux). Your own shell with tabs, splits, find and pinned tabs, and Kiri's `docker` first on the PATH.

## Fixed and improved
- **Kubernetes pods can use your own folders.** A pod's `hostPath` reaches your drives at `/mnt/c`, `/mnt/d` on Windows, `/Users` on the Mac and `/home` on Linux. Stop and start the cluster once to get it.
- **Linux: Kubernetes no longer breaks your terminals.** Privileged containers get their own `/dev`, as on Docker.
- **Containers keep their connections** while others start and stop.
- **Ports below 1024 and `ping` work without root,** as on Docker.
- **Container DNS keeps working** when the VM's resolver goes down, and `docker build` uses your Mac's DNS.
- **Deleting Kiri no longer breaks `docker build`.**
- **Firewall tools work in containers:** nftables, iptables, ipset, IPVS and traffic control.
- **A volume over part of a bind gets the image's files,** as on Docker. With `./:/app` and `/app/node_modules`, the container keeps its own Linux `node_modules`, not your computer's.
- **Kiri checks for updates every 6 hours** while it stays o

releases.name: Kiri 0.1.17
releases.body:
## Fixed
- **Turning off automatic updates now sticks.** On Mac, Windows and Linux, Settings showed **Off**, but the choice wasn't saved, so Kiri checked for updates again at the next launch. It's saved now.
- **Turning on crash reports sends only new crashes.** Switching them on used to send every crash still waiting, including ones you'd answered **Not now** to. Kiri now sends only crashes from after you turned reports on. You can still send an older one yourself from its card.
- **Logs and reports take out more secrets.** Passwords in URLs, `Authorization` values of any kind, PEM private keys, values after flags such as `--password`, GitHub, GitLab, Docker Hub and AWS access key tokens, and keys such as `PGPASS`, `API-KEY` and `*_PRIVATE_KEY` are now replaced with `[redacted]` before anything leaves your computer. It errs towards taking out too much: the whole user part of a URL goes, not only its password.
- **Windows: updates stay on HTTPS.** Kiri no longer follows a redirect from the update feed down to plain HTTP, and release builds no longer accept a feed from a local file.
- **Crash reports never carry your Kiri Cloud account.** A crash sent while you were signed in to Kir

releases.name: Kiri 0.1.15
releases.body:
## New
- **Linux: signed packages and repositories.** Every `.rpm` and the Linux checksums are signed with the Kiri Releases key, and download.runkiri.com now serves signed apt and dnf repositories, so `apt upgrade` and `dnf upgrade` can keep Kiri current. The key is `kiri-archive-key.asc` on the download site.

## Fixed
- **Mac: image files no longer come back empty.** When the engine went to sleep or stopped right after a pull, the VM could stop before its disk had caught up, and a newly unpacked image could keep its file names but lose their contents. Builds then failed in `RUN` steps and some programs (iperf3, for one) wouldn't start. Kiri now waits for the engine's VM to power off, writes each layer out in full before using it, and unpacks again any layer that was cut short.
- **`kiri share` no longer crashes when its output goes away.** Piping it into a command that exits, or closing the terminal it printed to, made it panic and leave a crash report. Kiri commands now end quietly when their output is closed.

---
Downloads for macOS, Windows and Linux: https://runkiri.com/releases/

releases.name: Kiri 0.1.14
releases.body:
## New
- **A fresh Kiri is quiet.** Nothing downloads and nothing new appears until you use it: the build engine (BuildKit) is fetched the first time you build, not at setup, and an empty Images list no longer offers a download.
- **The Engine card is your switch.** A fresh Kiri reads **Off** with **Start**, even while it sets itself up inside. Press **Start** and it reads **Running**, and stays Running while the engine rests between uses. Press **Stop** and it reads **Off**. A container you start yourself, for example with `docker run` in a terminal, also turns it to Running. The button is always there, and **Settings › Resources** has the same switch.
- **Linux: Kiri shows in software centers.** After installing the `.deb` or `.rpm`, Ubuntu's App Center, GNOME Software and KDE Discover list Kiri with its name, description and icon.

## Changed
- **Linux: installing doesn't start anything.** The engine starts when you set Kiri up (open Kiri, or `sudo kiri host-access $USER`), and then it waits asleep until you use it.
- **The engine starts asleep.** After setup, a restart or a login it doesn't run a VM nobody asked for; the first `docker` command, pull or Run wakes it in about a t

aiSummary.oneLiner: Minimalist static site generator built with Go.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Kiri is a fast, dependency-free static site generator that compiles Markdown into HTML. It uses standard Go templates for layout design, offering extreme flexibility. The tool is designed to be as fast as possible, enabling instant rebuilds during development. It supports frontmatter for metadata and generates RSS feeds automatically. Kiri focuses on simplicity, avoiding complex plugin systems in favor of convention.
keyFeatures: Markdown processing: converts standard Markdown files into static HTML pages.
Template engine: utilizes Go's native text/template for defining site layouts.
Live reload: includes a built-in development server that refreshes on file changes.
Asset bundling: copies static assets seamlessly to the output directory.
Fast execution: leverages Go's concurrency for extremely rapid build times.

useCases.title: Personal Blogs
useCases.description: Create and publish a fast, minimalist personal blog from Markdown files.

useCases.title: Documentation Sites
useCases.description: Generate technical documentation pages quickly without complex setups.

useCases.title: Portfolio Portals
useCases.description: Build lightweight portfolio websites showcasing projects and skills.

useCases.title: Landing Pages
useCases.description: Deploy simple product landing pages with minimal overhead.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers who prefer writing in Markdown and want a brutally simple, fast SSG. It requires basic knowledge of Go templates for customizing layouts.
